source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Flushing with tap water instead of a sterile solution, in order to more effectively clear whatever might be causing this resistance","B":"A push-pause technique, stopping if resistance is ever met, rather than pushing harder as the colleague is currently suggesting","C":"Forceful, rapid flushing without much regard for the resistance felt, similar to what the colleague is currently suggesting doing","D":"Fairly little flushing being needed for this particular device, contrary to why the nurse is performing this task in the first place"}}
source_row.rationale: Proper technique for flushing an intermittent IV access device (heparin/saline lock) includes using a "push-pause" method with an appropriate sterile flush solution (per facility protocol, which may include normal saline alone or with heparin), and stopping immediately if resistance is met — never forcing a flush against resistance, since this could dislodge a clot or cause other complications.
source_row.source_detail: IV access flushing: use prescribed sterile flush technique and never force against resistance; reviewed 2026-08-14.
source_row.source_name: Infusion Nurses Society — IV Flushing and Locking Standards
source_row.stem: A nurse is flushing a heparin lock to maintain patency and encounters some resistance partway through, though a colleague suggests just pushing a bit harder to clear whatever is blocking it. The nurse should instead use which technique?
